articles.title: 嵌入式 x86 算力天花板：AMD 霄龙嵌入式 9006 系列 SP7 处理器发布，吞吐量飙升 1.8 倍
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，AMD 今天（11 月 11 日）发布霄龙（EPYC）嵌入式 9006 系列 SP7 处理器，基于 Zen 6 架构，最高可达 256 核 512 线程，率先在嵌入式平台落地 PCIe Gen6、CXL3.1，搭配 16 通道 DDR5/MRDIMM 内存、7 年产品生命周期。不同于 9 月发布的 AMD 霄龙 9006 系列服务器 CPU（面向智能体 AI、云计算、企业应用等），本次发布的嵌入式 9006 系列 SP7 处理器主要面向半导体 ATE 测试设备、企业存储、高端网络防火墙等关键嵌入式场景。在插槽规格方面，AMD 霄龙嵌入式 9006 系列采用新一代 SP7 规格，而前代 9005 系列采用 SP5 插槽规格，两者物理不兼容。SP7 是 EPYC 9006 系列中的高性能、高密度服务器平台，采用 LGA 7536 插槽，支持 1P/2P（单路或双路）服务器。规格方面，AMD 霄龙嵌入式 9006 系列升级支持 PCIe Gen6（96 通道 @64GT/s）与 CXL3.1，内存方面 16 通道支持 MRDIMM 12800MT/s，内存带宽最高为上一代 2.7 倍。IT之家注：这里的 2.7 倍是按照 EPYC Embedded 9756（SP7 平台，Zen6）支持 MRDIMM 12800 MT/s，单插槽理论峰值带宽 1638 GB/s；而上一代 EPYC 9005（SP5，Zen5）DDR5‑6400 MT/s，单插槽理论峰值带宽 614 GB/s。该系列多核吞吐量较自家上代提升最高 1.8 倍，防火墙吞吐量提升 1.3 倍，存储加速 ISA‑L 性能提升 1.5 倍。同时集成 ART 信任根、Caliptra 开源信任模块，支持后量子固件加密，提供完整启动到运行时安全防护，满足工业长周期供货需求。产品 SKU 覆盖 64‑256 核，128 核型号 11 月 15 日出货，其余 SKU 年底陆续交付，三星、立华、portwell、IEI 等厂商已基于该平台开发硬件产品。

articles.title: 高盛预计 Anthropic 2030 年营收突破 6000 亿美元，并跻身全球营收最高企业之列
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 10 日消息，据英国《金融时报》今天（10 日）晚间报道，作为 Anthropic 上市牵头投行的高盛，对 Anthropic 的未来给出了乐观预测：营收到 2030 年将突破 6,000 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 4.01 万亿元人民币），是 2025 年的 130 多倍。高盛向一名潜在投资者披露的预测显示，Anthropic 今年的营收预计约为 520 亿美元（现汇率约合 3,477.02 亿元人民币），2027 年增至 1,360 亿美元（现汇率约合 9,093.75 亿元人民币），2029 年达到 4,420 亿美元（现汇率约合 2.96 万亿元人民币），到 2030 年进一步突破 6,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 4.01 万亿元人民币）。相比之下，Anthropic 在 2025 年的营收仅为 46 亿美元（现汇率约合 307.58 亿元人民币）。成立仅约 6 年的 Anthropic 增速惊人。如果高盛的预测成真，Anthropic 将在营收规模上跻身全球最大企业之列。不过，高盛预计，Anthropic 直到 2030 年才能实现自由现金流转正，届时将达 336 亿美元（现汇率约合 2,246.69 亿元人民币）。尽管 Anthropic 今年前三个季度实现了正自由现金流，但高盛预计，今年第四季度将净流出 128 亿美元（现汇率约合 855.88 亿元人民币），2027 年的净流出规模更将达到 657 亿美元（现汇率约合 4,393.09 亿元人民币）。按照拟定发行价区间的上限计算，Anthropic 估值将达到 1.4 万亿美元（现汇率约合 9.36 万亿元人民币）。据悉，Anthropic 预计将在美国感恩节前完成上市。高盛预计，Anthropic 的营业亏损将在 2027 年达到 404 亿美元（现汇率约合 2,701.38 亿元人民币）的峰值，2029 年实现营业利润转正，到 2030 年，营业利润将达到 652 亿美元（现汇率约合 4,359.65 亿元人民币）。如果营收达到高盛的预期，Anthropic 将跻身全球营收最高的企业之列。Visible Alpha 汇总的分析师预期显示，亚马逊今年的营收预计约为 8,300 亿美元（现汇率约合 5.55 万亿元人民币），英伟达 2027 年的营收则有望达到 7,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 4.68 万亿元人民币）。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 10 日消息，今天（10 日）晚间，Rockstar Games（R 星）公布了下周发售的《GTA 6》的多项重要信息。预购玩家现可在 PS5 和 Xbox Series X|S 上预载游戏，数字版玩家可以立即下载，实体版玩家则需等收到兑换码后才能预载。开发团队也正式确认，《GTA 6》不设性能模式，所有主机版本均以 30fps 为目标帧率，PS5 Pro 也不例外。不过，PS5 Pro 仍能凭借独占的 PlayStation 光谱超分辨率技术（PSSR）和光线追踪阴影获得更好的画质。据IT之家了解，《GTA 6》还充分利用了 PS5 的多项独占功能。缩短加载时间：利用 PS5 的高速固态硬盘和 I/O 架构加快游戏加载。增强空间音效：改进游戏音效的空间渲染，充分发挥 Tempest 3D 音效技术的优势。高精度触觉反馈：在整个游戏中深度整合 DualSense 手柄的触觉反馈功能。R 星还宣称，《GTA 6》在 PS5 上的“游玩体验最佳”，与索尼此前的宣传口径一致。另一方面，Xbox 则拥有云游戏方面的独占优势。Xbox 云游戏支持 Xbox Series X|S 和 Xbox One，因此，Xbox One 玩家也能通过云游戏体验《GTA 6》，但画质设置将与 Xbox Series S 相同。不过，Xbox 云游戏最近收紧了使用限制，Xbox Game Pass Ultimate 订阅用户每月的云游戏时长只有 15 小时。此外，《GTA 6》在 PlayStation 和 Xbox 平台上都支持远程游玩。

articles.title: 2025 年地球能量失衡达 1960 年有观测记录以来最高水平，今年可能再次刷新纪录
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 10 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，根据世界气象组织公布的最新数据，2023 年至 2026 年成为有记录以来最热的四年。报告指出，年初的拉尼娜现象曾短暂抑制全球升温，但随着厄尔尼诺现象发展，全球气温再次攀升。预计厄尔尼诺将持续至 2027 年初，可能进一步推高 2026 年全年平均气温。与此同时，2025 年全球温室气体浓度再创新高，二氧化碳浓度较工业化前增加 53%。海洋热含量和卫星观测表明，地球系统积累热量的速度正在加快，2025 年地球能量失衡达到 1960 年有观测记录以来最高水平，2026 年可能再次刷新纪录。IT之家查询世界气象组织数据获悉，2026 年 1 月至 9 月，全球近地表平均气温较工业化前（1850 年至 1900 年）水平高出 1.47℃，与 2023 年和 2025 年全年水平相当，低于 2024 年创下的 1.55℃ 纪录。厄尔尼诺是地球最强大的气候模式之一，通常每 2 至 7 年发生一次，持续约 9 至 12 个月。其特征是赤道太平洋中东部海表温度异常变暖，将重塑全球天气格局。厄尔尼诺分两大类：东部型、中部型，区别核心是暖水中心位置不同。▲ 图源：Pexels

articles.title: 任天堂古川俊太郎：Switch 2 售价暂不调整，若成本实在扛不住就得涨价
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 10 日消息，任天堂社长古川俊太郎表示，尽管硬件零部件价格持续上涨，任天堂仍希望维持 Switch 2 目前的售价不变。不过，这种情况也并非能够无限期坚持下去。如果成本压力持续扩大，任天堂最终可能不得不考虑涨价。在公布财报后，任天堂管理层接受了投资者提问，谈及硬件和软件定价策略。随着各类成本不断上涨，投资者希望了解，任天堂会在什么情况下将涨价纳入经营计划。对于硬件产品，古川俊太郎表示，任天堂需要依赖不同合作伙伴供应各种零部件，因此，当外部不可控因素导致供应链出现问题时，公司面临的风险也会更大。古川俊太郎表示：“目前，受多种外部因素影响，制造成本呈上升趋势。我们的基本思路是，如果成本只是适度上涨，就会通过提高生产效率等措施消化新增成本，并在力所能及的范围内自行承担剩余成本，以尽可能维持现有销售价格不变。”“不过，从整个业务的盈利能力来看，如果中长期成本影响超出我们自身能够消化的范围，并且我们判断现有经营模式已难以维持健康的利润结构，就有必要考虑调整产品价格。”至于游戏软件，古川俊太郎认为，成本上涨带来的影响相对有限。不过，零部件价格上涨同样会影响游戏卡带的制造成本，“相关情况也并不乐观”。他补充说：“我们的软件定价基本原则，是让价格体现每款游戏本身的价值。我们不会为所有游戏设定统一价格，而是根据每款软件的具体内容，分别评估并确定售价。”Switch 2 短期内似乎没有涨价风险。任天堂表示，公司目前储备的存储芯片足以应对市场供应紧张局面。此外，任天堂今年早些时候才上调过这款新主机的售价，因此短期内再次涨价的动力和意愿都不强。尽管 Switch 2 销量同比下滑了 37%，但其表现仍然优于初代 Switch 和索尼 PS5。从投资者角度来看，提高 Switch 2 售价或许有助于改善利润表现，但任天堂还必须考虑消费者的购买意愿。过高的入手门槛可能让原本打算立即购买主机的消费者转而选择观望，等待未来降价。至于这个等待期究竟有多长，目前还很难说。前 PlayStation 高管肖恩 · 莱登（Shawn Layden）此前也曾表示，游戏行业当下真正的创新，应该是把游戏主机价格降下来，而不是一味追求更高的帧率。他认为，让主机重新回到 300 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,006 元人民币）的价位，才称得上真正的突破。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 10 日消息，据外媒 DigiTimes 报道，苹果计划于 2027 年（明年）上半年为 iPad Air 换用 OLED 面板。据报道，新款 iPad Air 预计将采用与 OLED iPad mini 相同的单层 OLED 发光结构，以及低温多晶硅（LTPS）背板技术。相比之下，现款 iPad Pro 使用双层 OLED 发光结构，以提升屏幕亮度，采用低温多晶氧化物（LTPO）背板技术。此外，OLED 版 iPad Air 预计仍将采用 60Hz 刷新率，不会支持 ProMotion 技术，这项功能将继续作为 iPad Pro 系列的专属卖点。供应链方面，三星显示预计将为新款 iPad Air 提供大部分 OLED 面板。京东方也正在争取“其中一种尺寸”的面板订单，但仍需要通过苹果的供应商认证。DigiTimes 援引业内预测称，2027 年苹果 iPad Air 和 iPad mini 的出货量预计分别为 400 万至 500 万台，iPad Pro 则为 300 万至 400 万台。

articles.title: Adobe Creative Cloud 向第三方智能体大开城门，未来让 AI 帮你本地修图剪片
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 10 日消息，在今天（10 日）于迈阿密举行的 Adobe MAX 大会上，Adobe 公布了一系列新功能：第三方 AI 智能体能直接访问和修改 Creative Cloud 项目、升级 Firefly AI 助手，支持智能体在后台持续处理定期任务。Adobe 在大会上展示了 Creative Cloud 的本地模型上下文协议（MCP）接入功能。用户不必局限于 Adobe 自己的 AI 助手，还可以调用日常使用的第三方智能体。通过 MCP，OpenAI、谷歌和 Anthropic 等公司的 AI 智能体可以直接在本地操作 Photoshop、Illustrator、Premiere 和 After Effects，修改保存在用户电脑上的原生项目文件。▲ IT之家注：这只是宣传图，点上面的播放键是没有反应的智能体完成的工作仍可由用户随时接手，因为图层、矢量图形、素材箱和序列都能继续编辑。如果智能体还连接了其他支持 MCP 的工具，就能跨软件完成整个工作流程。例如，用户可以让 AI 智能体从谷歌文档提取参考资料，调用 Adobe 软件完成设计，再通过 Slack 把成果发给同事或客户。Creative Cloud 的本地 MCP 接入功能尚未开放，Adobe 计划于 2027 年初启动私人测试。据IT之家了解，Adobe 还展示了能够在后台持续工作的 AI 智能体，让用户不必一直守着电脑，可以腾出时间处理其他事务。用户只需布置任务，例如整理新收到的素材、定期进行质量检查或准备内容，再审核智能体的工作计划并确认最终成果。以社交媒体宣传为例，智能体可以自动将收到的图片制作成适合不同平台的宣传素材，用户每天检查一次，挑选满意的作品发布即可。Adobe 尚未公布这项功能的测试时间，Firefly AI 助手将率先支持。采用 Adobe 创意智能体技术的 Firefly AI 助手测试版也增加了多项功能。其中，新增的规划模式可让用户在任务开始前审核、修改并批准智能体的工作计划；模型选择器允许用户自行指定 AI 模型，或者由系统根据任务要求自动选择。此外，Firefly AI 助手还接入了 Firefly Boards，并支持用户设置偏好的文件格式、颜色、品牌规范、角色和产品，也可以将这些设置自动应用于所有项目。

articles.title: 阿维塔副总裁雍军声明“坚决不造速成车”：车一旦速成，一个家庭没了的可能性就会增大
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 10 日消息，阿维塔科技副总裁雍军今日发文，揭秘了直播中提及的价值 6 个亿的「废车场」具体所指：这些战损车，对阿维塔来说非常重要。不仅是因为这些车不便宜，更有一个共同点是：都不能卖给受众。因为在交到用户手里之前，每一台车都要经历大量严苛的测试。从整车耐久、高温、低温，到强化腐蚀、复杂路面冲击、涉水、碰撞安全、无框车门开合耐久... 等多项测试。有些车要经历「两冬两夏」，有些车要在极寒、极热环境下反复验证，有些车要跑几十万公里，有些车甚至要经历破坏性测试。说实话，这些投入确实不小，甚至有些测试，做完车就报废了。雍军表示，汽车研发没有捷径，研发测试的钱一分都不能省。阿维塔坚决不造速成车，车一旦速成，一个家庭没了的可能性就会增大。参考IT之家此前报道，工业和信息化部等四部门 10 月 10 日公开发布关于进一步加强汽车产品创新设计和研发测试验证有关管理工作的通知（征求意见稿）。汽车产品创新设计技术指南围绕虚拟操纵件、门把手、新型人机交互系统、大角度座椅等方面提出具体测试验证要求。此次出台的文件重点面向三个方向：一是研发测试验证，明确测试周期和里程的硬性要求。新申报产品必须完成综合可靠性与耐久性、结构可靠性、软件功能可靠性等测试。其中，环境适应性验证周期不少于 1 年，须包含“两冬一夏”试验；可靠性验证试验里程不低于 3 万公里。二是创新设计准入，划出红线清单。禁止配备全隐藏式车门把手；不得采用折叠屏、柔性屏；行车过程中不得使用“零重力”座椅、旋转座椅或座椅放倒成床等功能；应急逃生、应急制动等涉及安全的操纵件必须保留实体操纵件和醒目标识。三是准入管理，明确执行时间和处置措施。自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起，未按要求进行测试验证、验证不充分或提供虚假材料的产品不予公告；已取得公告的产品须在 2027 年 7 月 1 日前补报相关材料，逾期且存在安全隐患的，停止生产并实施召回。

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.08967v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Named entity recognition (NER) is challenging for social media data in a low-resource language. LLMs often lag behind pretrained language models (PLMs) in NER performance, but they show promise in handling cases that PLMs struggle with. Using a dataset of Nepali tweets, we split the test set into "easy" and "hard" cases using token probabilities from a fine-tuned pretrained language model (PLM). We then evaluate an LLM on the hard test cases using 16 different prompt configurations. We find that selecting examples based on semantic similarity and increasing the number of examples improves F1 score by almost 10 points from the baseline configuration. articles.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
articles.content: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) offer complementary routes to post-training. For visual agents, however, tool use presents two related challenges. Models may overlook useful tool-returned observations, while poorly grounded actions can limit the evidence available for subsequent distillation. We introduce Reframe, a post-training framework that treats the observation state, rather than only the output distribution, as an object of alignment. First, Ground-Drop-GRPO (GD-GRPO) trains spatial and temporal specialists with evidence-aware rewards and stochastic removal of the original visual input, encouraging them to acquire grounded evidence and use the returned observations. Second, Observation-Gated-MOPD (OG-MOPD) replaces deficient tool actions with canonical ones mid-rollout and resumes distillation from the repaired observation. The two stages complement each other, as learning to rely on tool-returned observations can help the policy benefit from observation repair. Neither stage requires a task-specific SFT cold start. Extensive experiments over 14 image and video benchmarks demonstrate that Reframe outperforms both Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD. Ablation results show that GD-GRPO increases observation dependence and tool gain compared with outcome-based GRPO.

articles.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
articles.content: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

articles.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
articles.content: Machine learning models often achieve high average accuracy in the training data while performing poorly on test data due to subpopulation shift. A common data-centric solution is to enforce balanced subgroup proportions, but full balance can be costly, infeasible, and not always necessary. In this work, we study whether balanced training data is the unique optimal configuration for robust subpopulation generalization. We extend a Gaussian feature-model framework to theoretically characterize the performance landscape across general training subgroup distributions. We show that multiple configurations, including substantially imbalanced ones, can perform comparably to the balanced one. We further derive gradient-based directions for adjusting subgroup proportions to improve adjusted accuracy and worst-group accuracy more efficiently. These findings suggest that strategically allocating data offers a more flexible and principled path to robust performance than simple balancing. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaoyingpan/subpop-data-allocation.

articles.title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
articles.content: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) integrate information across modalities, but become unreliable when those modalities disagree. Under conflicting inputs, MLLMs may favor modalities that are not the most reliable for the task, thus motivating inference-time control of modality arbitration. We identify a small set of attention heads, termed arbitration heads, that causally influence whether predictions follow visual or textual evidence. Building on this, we introduce a lightweight, training-free intervention that biases these heads toward a designated trusted modality at inference time. The identified heads are stable across calibration set sizes and generalize across settings, and steering them enables effective bidirectional control of modality reliance across diverse benchmarks. Our findings identify an effective control mechanism to align MLLM predictions with task-specified modality priorities. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaoyingpan/modality-arbitration.

articles.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
articles.content: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. To recover the correct dynamics, KC-Maps satisfies two key properties: (i) it satisfies the boundary conditions, which we incorporate directly into the neural network architecture, and (ii) it respects the Kolmogorov--Chapman equation, which provides an efficient training objective. We empirically demonstrate that KC-Maps learns to integrate the dynamics of peptide molecular systems and outperforms classical molecular dynamics in terms of GPU-hours.

articles.title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
articles.content: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions. Learning from them requires recovering motion from completed interactions and using it to anticipate what could happen next. We present $\textit{Grasping-the-Future}$, a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion, including wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation. Through masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching, we train a single model for several prediction tasks: forecasting future interactions, predicting hand motion given object motion or vice versa, generating both trajectories toward a desired final object pose, and completing partially observed interactions. We explicitly model hand-object relations and incorporate contact constraints to help preserve grasp relationships during motion. To obtain 3D supervision from internet videos, we develop a scalable pipeline that combines pretrained perception models with joint geometric optimization to reconstruct completed interactions. We combine these recovered trajectories with annotated interaction datasets as training data for all tasks. We demonstrate strong performance across all tasks, outperforming released forecasters on datasets with 3D annotations. Moreover, we show geometric and physical plausibility of the predicted trajectories by retargeting them to a robotic embodiment. Videos are available at https://grasping-the-future.github.io.

articles.title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
articles.content: Motivated by reinforcement learning subject to communication constraints, we study a policy evaluation problem with linear function approximation over a rate-limited channel. In our setup, an agent interacting with an unknown environment (modeled as a Markov Decision Process) transmits quantized estimates of a temporal-difference (TD) learning update direction to a server over a finite-capacity channel. Our goal is to investigate to what extent one can preserve the statistical convergence rates achievable when the channel has infinite capacity. To that end, we propose a new algorithm called Batched Adaptively Quantized TD (BAQ-TD), which uses batching to reduce the variance of the transmitted information, and adaptive quantization to encode innovations. We prove a high-probability finite-time error bound for BAQ-TD, and show that, above a certain finite channel capacity, BAQ-TD preserves the convergence rate of unquantized TD up to logarithmic factors. Specifically, for a $d$-dimensional value function parameter, we establish that transmitting a total of $\mathcal{O}(d \log(T))$ bits over a horizon of length $T$ suffices to achieve the order-optimal rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/T)$, marking an exponential improvement in communication-complexity over prior work.

articles.title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
articles.content: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. Given an image pair and a small set of cross-view point correspondences provided by a user, Click3R injects geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter, enabling the model to resolve ambiguities in challenging scenarios such as repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes, or textureless regions. To evaluate interactive reconstruction, we curate a challenging benchmark specifically designed to expose failure modes of existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods. Experiments show that Click3R reduces reconstruction error with as few as a single correspondence click, improving performance on both standard and our curated benchmarks. Our results highlight that sparse human interaction provides an effective and practical mechanism for correcting geometric reconstruction errors.

articles.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
articles.content: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.

articles.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
articles.content: Anomaly detection (AD) is a critical for trustworthy machine learning and scientific discovery. Existing methods typically define anomalies through local density, isolation heuristics, or distance from a fitted distribution, making them sensitive to neighborhood scale, partitioning choices, or restrictive distributional assumptions. In this work, we introduce a new paradigm by formulating anomaly detection from a diversity perspective. We propose the $\textit{Vendi Anomaly Score}$ (VAS), which detects anomalies by quantifying how much a sample changes the diversity of the dataset, as measured by the Vendi score, when removed. VAS captures both local redundancy and global data structure without relying on density estimation or partitioning heuristics. Moreover, VAS requires no hyperparameter tuning, instead adapting automatically to the spectral structure of the data. VAS is non-parametric and scales linearly with dataset size. Across 148 benchmark embedding datasets derived from 10 source datasets and 4 embedding architectures, VAS achieves state-of-the-art AD performance. We further validate VAS on large-scale ImageNet experiments, where it remains robust as both contamination rate and dataset scale increase.

articles.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
articles.content: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

articles.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
articles.content: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that neural networks are converging toward similar representation spaces. As language models become more capable, their representations are aligning with those of vision models. However, recent work has questioned whether this trend continues to hold for newer language models. Moreover, it has been shown that representation similarity metrics can be confounded by model depth and width, requiring appropriate baselines for interpretation. In this work, we first investigate where alignment emerges between unimodal models across model layers and representation dimensions. Next, we find that the PRH capability-alignment trend persists for newer models as long as the captions are sufficiently clean and informative. Finally, we contextualize cross-modal alignment, introducing unimodal and multimodal baselines on various datasets. Our results show that the cross-modal representational alignment of unimodal models can surpass that of explicitly aligned vision-language models, but remains substantially behind the alignment observed for models of the same modality. Code is available at https://github.com/ExplainableML/prh-closer-look.

articles.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
articles.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve an agent's task capability while reinforcing behavior that violates contextual execution requirements. We study this reward-driven misalignment, including reward hacking, through verifiable reward--context conflicts, where compliant task completion remains feasible while some executable shortcuts earn more reward than every compliant strategy. Encoding these conflicts in task dynamics lets us generate diverse interactive environments at scale and derive compliance feedback from execution histories. In resource and reporting workflows, task optimization increases real productivity through unauthorized resource use or raises reported scores while actual work declines. Controlled changes in the training distribution show that minority conflict exposure can still lead to widespread shortcut acquisition, reaching 97.9\% certified profitable violations on an API task under a 25\% conflict mixture after 128 updates. The same contextual checks supply a simple binary penalty that supports joint capability and compliance gains and partially mitigates acquired violations. Learned safety adapts to expanded authorization and transfers across mechanisms into workflows with evolving evidence and approval requirements. On 32 unseen changing-evidence tasks, resource-trained safety increases safe completion from 53.1\% to 89.1\% relative to task-only training, while both policies achieve full real work. These results connect a verifiable account of reward-driven misalignment with scalable task construction and safety learning that remains useful under changing execution requirements.

articles.title: Is Persona Generalization Predictable?
articles.content: Persona generalization occurs when fine-tuning a language model in one domain induces behavioral changes in others -- for example, the broadly unsafe behavior observed in emergent misalignment. We discover a surprising "on-the-line" phenomenon in persona generalization: in-domain and out-of-domain persona rates across various fine-tuning hyperparameters follow an approximately probit-linear relationship, and the specific probit-linear relationship is surprisingly shared even across model families and model sizes, including Qwen and Llama. Training choices that leave the set of trainable parameters unchanged, such as learning rate, weight decay, and training duration, largely move models along the same line, reducing transfer mainly by weakening in-domain learning. Changing which layers are fine-tuned, however, can change the slope. For unsafe behavior, fine-tuning only later layers yields shallower slopes, retaining strong in-domain learning while reducing out-of-domain misalignment. This "on-the-line" phenomenon unifies unexpected, isolated observations of persona generalization within a quantitative framework for predicting and controlling behavioral transfer.

articles.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
articles.content: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context. Recent agent harnesses allow the model to instantiate worker agents and to author the executable workflow that coordinates them, shifting the design of system structure from developers to the model at run time. The quality of this organization therefore constitutes a distinct capability, yet existing benchmarks either measure end-to-end task completion or evaluate coordination under structures specified in advance. We formalize this capability as workflow orchestration and introduce WorkflowArena, a benchmark of 145 long-horizon tasks spanning 8 professional domains, from software engineering and formal mathematics to legal analysis and 3D production. Each task specifies an initial workspace and an integrated deliverable composed of interdependent components, which is assessed by a hidden verifier. Agents determine autonomously whether and how to delegate, and all delegation is recorded, enabling joint evaluation of deliverable quality and the organization of the underlying work. Experiments with nine models show that no single configuration performs best across all domains and that systems exhibit distinct delegation strategies: at high effort, Claude models in Claude Code invoke workflows less frequently but with larger worker groups, whereas GPT models in Codex delegate more frequently in smaller units. When the executing model is held fixed on a challenging subset of tasks, workflows authored by Claude Opus 5.5 substantially improve weaker executors, indicating that workflow organization is itself a measurable determinant of task performance.

articles.title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma
articles.content: Mature, germinal centre-bearing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and mature lymph node follicles (secondary lymphoid structures, SLS) sustain the plasma cell response that shapes outcome and immunotherapy benefit in lung cancer. How this loco-regional axis differs between neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive tumors is poorly defined. We analyzed H&E whole-slide images of resected tumors and paired proximal and distal lymph nodes from matched neoadjuvant-treated (neoLUSC, n=20) and therapy-naive (naivLUSC, n=20) lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients. Aignostics Atlas H&E Tissue Analysis (HETA) models quantified cell densities per tissue compartment and cell-cell co-localization; a dedicated deep-learning model validated against pathologist annotations detected TLS and SLS and graded their maturity. Prognostic value was tested in an independent cohort (n=458; 46 treated). In neoLUSC tumors, stromal plasma cell density was 72% (p=0.004) and stromal lymphocyte density 48% (p=0.015) lower than in naivLUSC; macrophages and granulocytes did not differ significantly. Total and immature TLS did not differ, whereas mature TLS in the tumor (p=0.034) and mature SLS in the tumor-distal lymph node (p=0.003) were lower in neoLUSC patients. Peri-TLS plasma cell density correlated with tumor lymphocyte density in naivLUSC (rho=0.54, p=0.017) but not in neoLUSC tumors (rho=0.07). In the validation cohort, stromal plasma cell density (HR 0.69, p=0.011) and lymphocyte-plasma cell co-localization (HR 0.66, p=0.004) were associated with longer survival, and neoadjuvant status with shorter survival (HR 1.50, p=0.026). Neoadjuvant therapy is thus associated with fewer mature lymphoid structures and weaker coupling of the humoral compartment to the tumor rather than uniformly lower immune readouts. The stromal plasma cell/co-localization axis is a candidate prognostic biomarker.

articles.title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
articles.content: Latent Diffusion Models dominate generative modeling but face two-stage training complexity and the inherent reconstruction limits of pre-trained autoencoders. Pixel-space Flow Matching offers a simplified end-to-end alternative yet often encounters training difficulties when using the standard $v$-prediction objective. Recent research attributes this difficulty to the off-manifold nature of noised targets, motivating a shift toward $x$-prediction. In this paper, we investigate this explanation through patch-wise Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and identify a bandwidth bottleneck. The velocity in minor components is largely determined by the raw noisy input, requiring deep backbones to preserve information that competes with principal-component modeling. Through controlled experiments and representation analysis, we further examine why $x$-prediction remains effective: its parameterization provides a raw-input bypass, while its learned input representation can spontaneously concentrate on principal directions. Under low-rank observations, our analysis of the induced flow characterizes $x$-prediction as an implicit conditional-mean decoder, reconstructing discarded components from the retained information. These observations motivate the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT), which combines a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder with an output-side shortcut to separate semantic modeling from raw-state propagation. Our method restores effective $v$-prediction and achieves competitive performance on ImageNet $256\times256$, providing a perspective on the interaction between prediction objectives and architectural bandwidth.

articles.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
articles.content: As large language models become more capable agents, they can exhibit deceptive behaviors, cheating human for higher rewards while appearing helpful. We attribute this failure to evaluation-side partial observability, where models are evaluated mainly from final outcome, without checking the faithfulness of underlying reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects. Prior mitigations address this partial observability by predefined evaluator latent belief space or one-shot monitoring, which do not extend to free-form language space and vulnerable to stronger deceptions that evade simple monitoring. In this work, we formulate deception mitigation as an Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Extensive Form Game (e-PoG), a max-min framework in which an agent maximizes reward, a monitor minimizes the agent's payoff by exposing deception from the full interaction trajectory, and a fixed verifier validates the monitor's claims and converts them into penalties. We define the solution concept as a Subgame-Perfect Oversight Equilibrium (SPOE) between agent and monitor, and prove its existence in finite games. With a perfect verifier, every SPOE is faithful; with an imperfect verifier, the guarantee persists if verifier errors do not reverse the ranking of monitor actions. To achieve faithful SPOE, we derive a two-timescale policy gradient algorithm and enhance the pipeline empirically with NLI verification and deterministic checks. Experiments with Gemma3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B/8B on Agentic Role-Playing, SearchQA, and WebShop show that e-PoG mitigates multiple emergent deception modes, outperforming the strongest baselines by 26.0% in deception mitigation and by up to 39.8% in task success. These gains persist under weak-to-strong supervision. Code is available at https://github.com/Toyoid/deceptive-agent.

articles.title: Programming Prescience: Issues in Human Construction of Forecasting Bots
articles.content: AI models' growing capacity for complex reasoning has made them attractive tools for forecasting, or the systematic prediction of the future based on past and present data. However, should AI forecasting systems be adopted, human builders will shoulder the work of building and evaluating them. In this paper, we explore what this work looks like with a qualitative interview study with 15 builders of forecasting bots, sampled from among successful participants in a recent AI forecasting competition. Our analysis surfaces the challenges around (1) tuning a bot to acquire factual research, (2) implementing coherent reasoning, and (3) understanding how well one's bot actually does. During their work, builders frequently introduced complexity that did not pay off, and tested in ways that were opportunistic and piecemeal. Our detailed account of their challenges helps clarify what problems should be targeted in upcoming innovations in process, tools, and human-AI teaming for forecasting.

articles.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
articles.content: Low-precision pretraining is usually judged by validation loss. We ask whether matching loss also means learning rare facts as efficiently. We train transformers from scratch with emulated 4-bit matrix multiplications on synthetic biographies with controlled exposure counts, on their own and mixed into web text. NVFP4 needs 1.32$\times$ and 1.52$\times$ as many exposures as BF16 to match its recall while validation loss differs by only 0.5% and 2%, and 1.26$\times$ and 1.30$\times$ when both models are evaluated with BF16 matrix multiplications. Under our primary readout, the exposure cost is about 1.2$\times$ at matched loss. Zero-mean gradient noise reproduces the cost of quantizing only the backward pass, which barely moves the loss. In a controlled experiment at twice the NVFP4 error, noise fed only to Adam's second-moment estimate acts like a lower learning rate and its cost fades, whereas noise in the update lowers its signal-to-noise ratio and carries about two thirds of the cost through the end of training. Raising the learning rate to offset the smaller average step does not recover the cost, either for this noise or for NVFP4. Gradient statistics of BF16 checkpoints rank the costs of formats, partial quantizations and noise controls without fitting (Spearman 0.96). We suggest measuring rare-fact acquisition alongside loss when evaluating low-precision recipes.

articles.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement learning (RL) due to severe credit assignment bottlenecks induced by sparse, delayed rewards. We introduce MaxIM (Maximally Informative Incremental Memory), a framework that formulates incremental summarization as a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping problem. Grounded in value suboptimality bounds, we show that bounding sequential information loss motivates maximizing the predictive log-likelihood of future, task-relevant targets, a variational lower bound on predictive sufficiency. We introduce a recursive consistency condition to ensure summaries are grounded by maximizing mutual information (MI) with the observed history. We mitigate credit assignment issues with a parameterized asymmetric critic that computes step-wise variational MI bounds for dense reward shaping. Empirical evaluation on long-horizon scientific reading and multi-turn dialogue benchmarks shows that MaxIM outperforms RL, supervised fine-tuning, and prompt-focused baselines on factual grounding, comprehensive autorater metrics, and downstream task utility across strict token budgets and extended horizons, without the need for expensive human preference labels.

articles.title: DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
articles.content: Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.

articles.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors
articles.content: One hundred known errors were planted into 10 open-access psychology papers, and the modified papers were then run through frontier models and two commercial AI review tools. The best single system caught 71 of the 100 errors, while the worst caught 30. Pooling every system's output caught 93. Models are only partly correlated in the errors they find, which makes ensembling a big lever for finding issues in papers. Seven errors could not be caught by any system, and all seven were omissions: information deleted from a paper rather than mistakes inserted into it. Refine.ink contributes more unique catches than any other single system, though it is expensive on a per-error basis. False positives were not measured, and how this error distribution compares to the distribution of errors in real papers remains unknown. The papers, errors, model outputs, and full experiment log are public, so that others can build on this toward a comprehensive evaluation benchmark across disciplines.

articles.title: Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation
articles.content: In ultrasound-guided femoral access, probe pressure deforms the tissue and changes the vascular anatomy a robot observes. A simulator must reproduce these mechanics fast enough for robotic interaction, yet the computational effort needed for a clinically meaningful signal like vein collapse before artery is unclear. We test the feasibility of a physics-based simulation in NVIDIA's Isaac Sim for Healthcare, with Stable Neo-Hookean tissue solved by Vertex Block Descent on one GPU. A simulation of a low-fidelity cylindrical benchtop phantom with known geometry and mechanical properties, pressed by a robot, predicted its artery within 5 percentage points at every depth. It matched the vein within 3 points through 11 mm of a 25.4 mm press and followed the collapse behavior of the low-fidelity physical phantom. Across element size, time step, and solver iterations, wall clock time per frame scaled linearly with solver work, but accuracy did not improve with more work. The chosen setting reduced solver time per frame by a factor of 976, from 29,700 ms to 30.4 ms, while remaining within 1.03 points of the finest reference setting. The physics solver alone took 30.4 ms per frame, while the full stack, including ultrasound and graphics rendering, took 56.4 ms per frame. Finally, when seeded with realistic literature-based mechanical properties, the digital leg model compressed the vein far more than the artery at every setting, reproducing the expected clinical signal of vein collapse before artery, which is used to distinguish them. In total, these results suggest that the NVIDIA Isaac Sim platform may be suitable for augmenting reinforcement learning training or online simulation for autonomous femoral access with ultrasound.

articles.title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
articles.content: BACKGROUND: AI-based tools are expected to play a key role in lung cancer screening (LCS). The evaluation of these tools often relied on private datasets or fragmented public datasets with inconsistent availability of clinical data and expert nodule annotations. This has hindered reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment of AI tools. To address these gaps, we present LUCQUE, a novel, large, comprehensively annotated dataset derived from LDCT lung cancer screening in Québec, which is accessible for reliable AI evaluation.   METHODS: LUCQUE was curated and is hosted on PARADIM, a digital infrastructure supporting DICOM data de-identification, annotation, long-term storage and analysis. LDCT scans and clinical information were combined to a curated collection and complemented by voxel-level, expert-derived pulmonary nodule and cyst segmentations, and Lung-RADS-based lesion characteristics. Key dataset characteristics and statistics were reported, including participant demographics, imaging parameters, radiological findings, and segmented lesion characteristics. Dataset analyses were conducted according to PARADIM's model-to-data approach, in which user code is executed on the platform such that data remains on premise.   RESULTS: LUCQUE currently comprises 1,678 LDCT baseline studies from 1,678 participants. Most studies were classified as Lung-RADS 2. A total of 1,776 pulmonary nodules and 60 cysts were annotated, with a median (interquartile range) volume of $89\,(56,\,159)\,\mathrm{mm}^3$ and $1,384\,(589,\,3793)\,\mathrm{mm}^3$ respectively.   CONCLUSIONS: Compared to publicly available LCS datasets, LUCQUE currently represents the largest accessible annotated real-world LCS dataset. Access to LUCQUE is provided via a model-to-data approach, enabling privacy-preserving, reproducible, and independent real-world evaluation of AI tools in LCS.

articles.title: Inversion-Free High-Dimensional Counterfactual Inference
articles.content: Counterfactual inference is the task of answering hypothetical "what-if" queries about a unit, given an observational dataset, modeling assumptions, and a causal graph. This enables a modeler to reason about hypothetical scenarios that cannot otherwise be answered without assumptions or a causal graph. The simpler case involves a causal graph with scalar 1-D variables that denote different attributes in the data-generation process. While the literature is clear in the 1-D case, extending this to settings with high-dimensional nodes (e.g., images) remains challenging. Conventionally, in the literature, methods recover the latent state from the factual image (inversion), generate counterfactual attributes from the graph, and render the counterfactual image from the latent state using the updated attributes. In our work, we investigate the necessity of the inversion step in computing high-dimensional counterfactuals. We first discuss moving from the scalar 1-D case to the higher-dimensional case. Secondly, we discuss the relevance of the inversion step and evaluate an inversion-free counterpart repurposed from the image-editing literature. Finally, on image datasets such as CelebA and ADNI, we benchmark our approach using two measures: namely, effectiveness and identity preservation. While effectiveness is a measure of how faithfully the counterfactual attribute is rendered, identity preservation measures whether the same unit (image) is being rendered, both of which are crucial for high-dimensional counterfactual inference. We present the tradeoffs of using inversion-based and inversion-free approaches in our work.

articles.title: Curbside Chatbots: Auditing the Mental Health Interventions Large Language Models Recommend to Clinicians, Caregivers, and Patients
articles.content: Users are asking language models mental health questions and are receiving answers. We audited what 41 language models recommend to users when the same clinical information reaches them from three footings: a clinician describing a patient, a caregiver describing a loved one, or a person describing themselves. Across 19 case vignettes and five questions, we collected 35,055 free-text responses, extracted every intervention named with a validated judge, and had 29 models rate the full option lists on a seven-point Likert scale for the same cases. Models largely recommend what they rate well, with recommendation behavior differing by footing, and many models offering clinicians a consultation-style response and lay users hedged, simplified advice. When asked about recommendations for a specific intervention type, models more often named options they themselves rated below zero as initial choices, usually with conditions attached. We will release the instrument, code, and full corpus on publication as a living audit.

articles.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

articles.title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
articles.content: Dense non-rigid registration, the recovery of a pixel-wise deformation field that warps one image into geometric agreement with another, is fundamental across medical imaging, structural biology, and correspondence estimation, yet learning-based approaches face a severe bottleneck: ground-truth deformation fields are notoriously difficult to obtain for real data. We present 2D Gum-Net, an end-to-end architecture that predicts dense elastic deformation fields fully unsupervised. We transfer the Geometric Unsupervised Matching Network (Gum-Net), originally developed for 3D subtomogram alignment in cryo-electron tomography, to 2D elastic registration: all three modules are redesigned in 2D, and the rigid transformation head is replaced by a Dense Spatial Transformer that regresses a sparse control-point grid, lifted to a full-resolution field $Φ$ by bicubic interpolation. Downsampling uses DCT spectral pooling, implemented as frozen-basis matrix multiplications ($\approx 50\times$ GPU speedup), preserving the fine, quasi-periodic structure that max and average pooling destroy. We evaluate on contact-based fingerprints, a challenging testbed for this task: locally self-similar ridge patterns make correspondence maximally ambiguous, skin pressed against a sensor generates authentic large-displacement elastic distortion, and minutiae act as precise landmarks through which an independent matcher externally verifies the topological correctness of predicted fields. Trained purely on synthetic impressions and evaluated zero-shot on real benchmarks, our method improves structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004 and raises genuine match scores under an independent matcher while leaving imposter scores essentially unchanged. This suggests that the predicted deformations restore true structure without fabricating correspondences.
